headline: Critical PHP2Shell Flaws Leaked; CISA Warns of Actively Exploited Bugs
summary: This cybersecurity brief for October 21, 2026, covers several critical developments. Details of two maximum-severity PHP vulnerabilities, dubbed "PHP2Shell," were leaked ahead of patches, with active exploitation already observed. CISA added six flaws to its KEV catalog, including the "Plex2Shell" chain. Meanwhile, the Lazarus APT group launched a new campaign using post-quantum cryptography, and a joint advisory warned of the highly active SafePay ransomware gang. Other major incidents include a ConnectWise supply chain attack impacting Microsoft 365 customers and an emergency revocation of eMudhra certificates due to weak private keys.

articles.headline: Ransomware Attacks Reached a Record High in August 2026
articles.title: Ransomware Attacks Hit Record High, NCC Group Reports
articles.excerpt: According to a new report from NCC Group, global ransomware attacks surged to a 2026 record in August, victimizing 1,073 organizations. This marks a 12% increase from July and a significant year-over-year rise. The industrial sector was the most frequent target, and the Qilin and The Gentlemen ransomware groups were the most prolific actors during the month.
articles.updateSummary: Ransomware attacks surged 50% in Q3 2026, reaching nearly 2,900 incidents, driven by intense rivalry between The Gentlemen and Qilin groups.
articles.updateContent: A new report from Nord Security reveals a significant escalation in ransomware activity during Q3 2026, with 2,894 attacks documented between July and September. This marks a 50% year-over-year increase and an 8.6% rise from Q2. The surge is primarily attributed to fierce competition between the two most dominant ransomware groups, The Gentlemen (383 attacks) and Qilin (363 attacks), who together accounted for over 25% of all incidents. This rivalry is driving innovation in TTPs and increasing operational tempo, suggesting a new phase of heightened activity in the ransomware landscape.

articles.headline: ConnectWise Shuts Down Cloud Services After Supply Chain Attack
articles.title: ConnectWise Supply Chain Attack Disrupts Cloud Services, M365
articles.excerpt: IT software provider ConnectWise has suspended its Cloud Backup, SaaS Security, and Cloud Management services following a significant supply-chain attack. The incident involved a compromised application credential for its multitenant OAuth application, which threat actors used to gain unauthorized, high-privilege access to the Microsoft 365 environments of its Managed Service Provider (MSP) partners and their customers. The attack bypassed user-based MFA, leading ConnectWise to take services offline and reset credentials.
articles.updateSummary: ConnectWise attack scope widens to nearly 1,000 M365 tenants, over 300 confirmed compromised.
articles.updateContent: New reports indicate the ConnectWise supply chain attack has a significantly wider reach than initially reported. Security firm Huntress now observes malicious sign-ins across nearly 1,000 Microsoft 365 tenants, with over 300 confirmed successful compromises. This expands the potential impact beyond the previously identified 162 tenants. The attacker gained access to sensitive data in Exchange, Teams, and SharePoint via a compromised API secret for the Cloud Backup service.

articles.headline: Critical PHP2Shell RCE Flaws Leaked Ahead of Coordinated Patch
articles.title: Critical PHP2Shell RCE Flaws (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619)
articles.excerpt: Two critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities in PHP, collectively named "PHP2Shell," were prematurely disclosed before a scheduled patch release. The flaws, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, affect a vast range of PHP versions from 5.4 onwards, placing a majority of the web at risk. Security researchers have reproduced the exploit, and Cloudflare has already detected initial attack attempts in the wild. Organizations are urged to prepare for immediate patching as soon as the official fixes are released to mitigate the threat of widespread server compromise.

articles.headline: CISA Adds Six Flaws to KEV Catalog, Including Plex2Shell Chain
articles.title: CISA KEV Catalog Updated with Six Actively Exploited Flaws
articles.excerpt: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added six new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, confirming they are under active attack. The update includes four flaws in Plex Media Server, collectively known as "Plex2Shell," which attackers are chaining for unauthenticated RCE to deploy malware. Vulnerabilities in Siemens Software Center and EG Secure Solutions SiteGuard Server Edition were also added. Federal agencies are mandated to patch these flaws by early November 2026.

articles.headline: Lazarus APT Uses AI and Post-Quantum Crypto in New Campaign
articles.title: Lazarus Group's "Operation FlashHole" Targets South Korea
articles.excerpt: The North Korean Lazarus APT group has launched a sophisticated cyberespionage campaign named "Operation FlashHole," targeting South Korean entities since July 2025. Researchers at Kaspersky revealed the campaign uses AI-generated content for spear-phishing lures, abuses legitimate South Korean software for initial access, and deploys new malware. Most notably, the group is using post-quantum cryptography (ML-KEM-1024) to encrypt its command-and-control communications, demonstrating a significant advancement in future-proofing its operations against decryption.

articles.headline: Advisory Warns of Prolific SafePay Ransomware Targeting Critical Infrastructure
articles.title: CISA, FBI Warn of Active SafePay Ransomware Attacks
articles.excerpt: CISA, the FBI, and international partners issued a joint advisory on the SafePay ransomware group, one of the most active operations of 2026. Since August 2024, the group has compromised approximately 600 organizations, including critical infrastructure sectors, across the Americas, Europe, and Australia. The advisory details the gang's common TTPs, which include credential theft, exploiting known vulnerabilities, and phishing. Agencies urge organizations to implement MFA, patch vulnerabilities, and maintain offline backups to defend against this widespread threat.

articles.headline: Weak eMudhra Certificate Keys Force Emergency Browser Blocks
articles.title: eMudhra Certificate Compromise Due to Weak Private Keys
articles.excerpt: A major internet security incident occurred after eight intermediate certificates from Indian Certificate Authority (CA) eMudhra were discovered to have critically weak private keys. The flaw, caused by insufficient randomness during key generation, allowed private keys to be recovered almost instantly. In one case, the private key was a single digit. This vulnerability enabled potential man-in-the-middle attacks and certificate forgery, forcing major browser vendors like Mozilla, Google, and Apple to issue emergency updates to distrust and revoke the compromised certificates, protecting users from potential impersonation attacks.

articles.headline: Arizona's IMS Care Center Discloses Breach of Patient Data
articles.title: IMS Care Center Discloses Patient Data Breach from Email System
articles.excerpt: IMS Care Center, a large physician-owned medical group in Arizona, has disclosed a data breach affecting its patients. The incident, which occurred in June 2026, involved unauthorized access to the company's corporate email system. An investigation completed in late September determined that sensitive patient information, including names, addresses, Social Security numbers, and medical data, was potentially exposed. The healthcare provider is now notifying affected individuals and offering complimentary credit monitoring services.

articles.headline: Critical RCE Vulnerabilities in PHP Affect Millions of Web Servers
articles.title: PHP Critical RCE Flaws: CVE-2026-109618 & CVE-2026-109619
articles.excerpt: Two critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, have been disclosed in PHP, a ubiquitous server-side scripting language. Both vulnerabilities carry a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2, indicating a high risk of exploitation. According to Palo Alto Networks' Cortex Xpanse, over 22.6 million internet-exposed instances are potentially vulnerable. Proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit code is reportedly available, and at least one European government has taken its website offline as a precautionary measure. Immediate patching is strongly recommended for all organizations using PHP to prevent potential server compromise, data theft, or malware deployment.
